answer: Reputation-shadow pricing. Each identity pays fees scaled by the ridge between its demonstrated history and the network median; new identities start on a low knoll of credit but any cluster of near-identical sparse histories triggers a steep marginal price. Every additional linked identity raises the next one's onboarding cost superlinearly, so a sybil farm of n identities pays roughly n² in fees. Honest agents grow out of the shadow by sustained distinct activity, like a willow rooting slowly.
